aboutPage.title: About Aakash Das
introParagraphs: I'm Aakash Das, a Nepal-based finance educator, content creator, and founder of RisePaisa. I work at the intersection of finance, technology, and education, making complex financial topics easier to understand through practical content and digital learning resources.

My work focuses on Nepal's financial system, including personal finance, banking, taxation, fintech, financial literacy, and the stock market. Through RisePaisa, I aim to make reliable financial knowledge more accessible and help students, young professionals, and everyday learners make better-informed financial decisions.
Alongside my work in finance education, I'm studying Information Technology and exploring how technology can improve the way people learn, access information, and manage their finances.

resources.title: Starter Personal Budget Framework
resources.description: A clean, structured monthly budgeting template designed for Nepali students and young professionals managing living expenses, emergency savings, and discretionary cash flow.
resources.author: Aakash Das
resources.contentHtml:
What’s Included

  • ✓Zero-based income and expense allocation formula adapted for monthly cash flows
  • ✓Dedicated emergency fund milestone tracker with customizable targets
  • ✓Discretionary spending categories tailored for urban living in Nepal
  • ✓Automated visual tables summarizing necessity vs. lifestyle ratios

Intended For

Students and early-career professionals in Nepal starting personal budgeting.

Framework Principles & Cash Flow Mechanics

Personal budgeting is not about restriction—it is about intentional capital allocation. In Nepal, young professionals and students often experience irregular cash flows from freelance projects, allowances, or entry-level stipends. This framework applies a zero-based cash allocation methodology adapted for living expenses in Kathmandu and urban centers.

A budget tells your money where to go instead of wondering where it went. — Core principle of zero-based financial allocation

Recommended Cash Flow Allocation Model

We recommend dividing incoming monthly cash flow into three core buckets before committing to discretionary purchases:

  • Fixed Baseline Needs (50%): Housing rent, internet, mobile recharge, groceries, and local commute.
  • Emergency & Future Reserves (30%): Liquid bank emergency reserve, health contingencies, and long-term savings.
  • Discretionary & Cultural (20%): Social dining, festivals, family obligations, and personal development.
Spending Category Recommended Share Kathmandu Baseline (NPR 30,000) Tracking Frequency
Fixed Essentials & Rent 50% NPR 15,000 Monthly recurring
Liquid Emergency Reserve 20% NPR 6,000 Per income cycle
Skill Building & Books 10% NPR 3,000 Flexible monthly
Discretionary & Social 20% NPR 6,000 Weekly reviewed
Rule of Thumb for Emergency Reserves

Always accumulate at least 3 months of baseline non-negotiable living costs in an easily accessible Class-A commercial bank savings account before investing in illiquid or high-risk vehicles.

Step-by-Step Implementation Guide

  1. Calculate your net realized monthly income across all verified sources.
  2. List all contractual fixed commitments (room rent, electricity, ISP, mobile recharge).
  3. Set aside your savings allocation immediately on payday rather than budgeting from what remains at month-end.
  4. Distribute remaining discretionary funds across 4 weekly spending envelopes.

resources.title: Nepal Banking & Account Checklist
resources.description: A practical evaluation guide for comparing commercial bank savings accounts, mobile banking charges, debit card fees, and digital transaction limits across banks in Nepal.
resources.author: Aakash Das
resources.contentHtml:
What’s Included

  • ✓Core documentation and KYC verification checklist for Nepali banks
  • ✓Standard fee schedules and annual maintenance charges across Class-A banks
  • ✓Transaction limits, mobile banking security rules, and ConnectIPS best practices
  • ✓Step-by-step checklist to evaluate bank interest tiers without marketing bias

Intended For

Anyone opening, reviewing, or consolidating personal bank accounts in Nepal.

Navigating Retail Banking in Nepal

Choosing the right commercial bank (Class-A) in Nepal involves balancing branch convenience, mobile banking platform stability, and hidden annual maintenance fees. Many account holders unknowingly incur debit card renewal fees, SMS alert charges, and interbank transfer commissions that silently erode low-balance savings.

Key Comparison Metrics & Regulatory Benchmarks

Service / Feature Standard Bank Range Recommended Threshold Watchout
Minimum Balance Requirement NPR 0 – 5,000 NPR 0 (Zero balance) Penalty charges for low balance
Mobile Banking Annual Fee NPR 250 – 500 Free or capped under NPR 300 Auto-deducted from account
Debit Card Issuance / Renewal NPR 350 – 600 / year Under NPR 400 Multi-year bundle charges
ConnectIPS Transfer Cap Up to NPR 2,000,000 / day Standard NRB limit Tiered per-transaction charge (NPR 2–8)
Student Account Privilege

Most Class-A commercial banks in Nepal offer dedicated Student Savings Accounts with zero minimum balance requirements and waivers on first-year mobile banking charges upon showing a valid college ID card.

Opening Your Account: Essential Verification Sequence

  1. Verify your National Identity Card (NID) or Citizenship certificate details with clear scanned copies.
  2. Obtain a recommendation letter or college ID if applying for a concessionary student account.
  3. Register for ConnectIPS directly through self-verification or bank branch linking.
  4. Set up biometric or two-factor authentication on mobile banking apps immediately upon activation.

resources.title: Student Productivity & Semester Tracker
resources.description: A minimal workspace template for organizing university modules, assignment deadlines, self-directed research notes, and weekly study targets.
resources.author: Aakash Das
resources.contentHtml:
What’s Included

  • ✓Semester module database tracking credits, professors, and class schedules
  • ✓Weekly assignment deadline board prioritizing deliverables by urgency
  • ✓Structured lecture notes capture framework with active recall sections
  • ✓Focus session tracker designed to eliminate digital study distractions

Intended For

College and university students managing multiple academic modules and deadlines.

Academic Workflow Architecture

Balancing coursework, college laboratory assignments, and personal skill development requires a systematic tracking system. Rather than keeping deadlines in your head or fragmented across chat apps, this tracker establishes a single source of truth for your semester.

Structure liberates creativity. When your deadlines are managed systematically, you have mental bandwidth to actually learn. — Academic workflow principle

Weekly Planning Cadence

  • Sunday Planning Session (20 minutes): Review upcoming assignment deliverables and lecture schedules.
  • Daily 3-Priority Rule: Define only three major academic objectives per morning.
  • Mid-Week Buffer Block: Allocate 90 minutes on Wednesdays to absorb overflow or difficult lab reports.
  • Friday Reflection & Archiving: File completed assignment documents and update progress status.
Module Deliverable Urgency Tier Preparation Window Review Checklist
Laboratory Report / Practical High (Weekly) 2 days prior to lab Code compile check & outputs
Mid-Term Coursework Essay Medium (Monthly) 10 days prior Reference citation & outline
Final Capstone Project High (Ongoing) Weekly sprint reviews Git commits & documentation
Self-Study / External Skills Continuous 1 hour daily block Project implementation
Beware Deadline Compression

Never schedule final submission uploads within 1 hour of university portal closing. Server congestion and ISP drops frequently cause unsubmitted penalties.

journals.title: Building Something That Matters
journals.excerpt: Building RisePaisa started from a simple frustration: financial information in Nepal was either overly academic or buried in difficult legal language. We wanted to build something clear, practical, and genuinely useful for everyday people.
journals.author: Aakash Das

content.lead: Building RisePaisa started from a simple, personal frustration. Whenever friends, relatives, or classmates had questions about banking, taxes, or stock investing in Nepal, they faced a frustrating choice: either read through dense government acts and circulars, or rely on second-hand hearsay from social media. There was almost nothing in between.

sections.heading: The Gap in Financial Literacy
paragraphs: Nepal has witnessed incredible technological progress over the past five years. Almost everyone carries a smartphone, and QR-based digital payments have become an everyday convenience. Yet our educational system rarely teaches the foundational mechanics of money management.

Many young people earn their first salary without knowing how social security deductions work, how income tax brackets are calculated, or what the difference is between saving and investing. We realized that access to digital money without financial education creates vulnerability rather than security.

sections.heading: Designing for Practical Utility
paragraphs: When we conceptualized the resources for RisePaisa, our guiding rule was utility. An article that explains a financial concept is fine, but a practical budget framework spreadsheet or a step-by-step banking checklist that someone can actually download and use that afternoon is ten times more valuable.

Designing these resources requires restraint. We strip away theoretical fluff and focus entirely on clarity. If a beginner cannot understand the first two paragraphs, the explanation has failed, no matter how technically accurate it might be.
sections.quote: Simplicity is not the absence of depth; it is the mastery of clarity.

sections.heading: The Patience Required to Build
paragraphs: Creating educational tools is not a fast game. There are no sudden viral shortcuts to earning trust. It requires consistently researching regulations, verifying numbers with qualified practitioners, and iterating based on how real people use the tools.

Building something that matters in Nepal means choosing steady, patient compounding over short-term vanity metrics. Every person who makes a better financial decision because of a guide we published makes the effort worthwhile.

Designing these resources requires restraint. We strip away theoretical fluff and focus entirely on clarity. If a beginner cannot understand the first two paragraphs, the explanation has failed, no matter how technically accurate it might be.

Simplicity is not the absence of depth; it is the mastery of clarity.

Creating educational tools is not a fast game. There are no sudden viral shortcuts to earning trust. It requires consistently researching regulations, verifying numbers with qualified practitioners, and iterating based on how real people use the tools.

Building something that matters in Nepal means choosing steady, patient compounding over short-term vanity metrics. Every person who makes a better financial decision because of a guide we published makes the effort worthwhile.

journals.excerpt: There is a distinct advantage in being a beginner: you ask the questions that experienced people often overlook. Embracing the discomfort of starting from scratch has been the most reliable driver of my own growth.
journals.author: Aakash Das

content.lead: Starting anything new involves an uncomfortable period of awkward incompetence. When you begin writing, your prose feels stiff. When you start coding, simple syntax errors consume hours. When you study a new domain, the sheer volume of unfamiliar terminology can feel intimidating. Most people stop here to protect their egos.

sections.heading: The Beginner’s Advantage
paragraphs: Zen philosophy speaks of "shoshin"—the beginner’s mind. In the beginner’s mind there are many possibilities, but in the expert’s mind there are few. When you have not yet formed rigid habits or dogmatic beliefs about how things "must" be done, you look at problems with fresh eyes.

In my own journey transitioning from accounting studies towards computer science and digital content creation, being a novice forced me to break everything down to first principles. I could not rely on memorized scripts; I had to understand the underlying mechanisms.

sections.heading: Consistency Over Intensity
paragraphs: Early in any pursuit, there is a temptation to attempt heroic bursts of effort: studying for fourteen hours straight or attempting an ambitious project in a single weekend. Almost always, this leads to burnout and quiet abandonment.

What actually compounds is quiet, unglamorous consistency. Reading for forty-five minutes every morning, writing one thoughtful page, or debugging one function daily creates an exponential curve that is invisible in the short run but unstoppable over three years.
sections.quote: Patience with the process; impatience with daily action.

sections.heading: Long-Term Games in a Short-Term World
paragraphs: Our digital environment constantly tempts us into short-term comparison. We see someone else’s highlight reel and feel behind. But when you adopt a decade-long horizon, the urgency to prove yourself today fades.
Being a beginner is not a temporary weakness to be hurried through; it is an active posture of curiosity that keeps you adaptable for the rest of your life.

journals.title: Where Finance Meets Technology
journals.excerpt: Nepal's shift from cash to QR codes and digital wallets happened faster than anyone predicted. Yet digital payments are only the foundation. The real opportunity lies in bridging digital access with actual financial literacy.
journals.author: Aakash Das

content.lead: If you walk through the streets of Kathmandu today, you will see QR payment stands at tea stalls, grocery vendors, and tempo drivers. The speed at which Nepal transitioned from cash-dominated commerce to seamless digital transactions is one of the most remarkable stories of technological adoption in South Asia.

sections.heading: Infrastructure Outpacing Understanding
paragraphs: While our transactional infrastructure has leapfrogged ahead, our collective financial understanding remains in its early stages. Frictionless payments make spending money easier than ever before. When transactions were physical, counting paper notes created a natural psychological pause. Digital payments remove that friction entirely.

Without disciplined personal accounting habits, digital convenience can inadvertently lead to higher lifestyle inflation and unmonitored expenditure. The technology has evolved, but human behavioral psychology remains unchanged.

sections.heading: The Next Wave of Nepali Fintech
paragraphs: The first era of fintech in Nepal was defined by rails: payment gateways, wallet integrations, and digital inter-bank transfers. That was necessary groundwork, and companies like Fonepay, eSewa, and Khalti built that foundation admirably.

I believe the next era will be defined by intelligence and guidance. How can software help a small business owner forecast cash flow? How can digital tools help a college student automate disciplined savings? How can retail investors analyze NEPSE company filings with clean, structured interfaces instead of clunky PDFs?
sections.quote: The true promise of fintech is not making spending faster; it is making financial well-being accessible.

sections.heading: Why This Matters for Young Builders
paragraphs: For students and engineers working in Nepal today, the intersection of finance and software offers an immense frontier. We do not need to simply clone foreign products. We have unique regulatory frameworks, cooperative banking networks, and cultural remittance dynamics that demand custom, home-grown solutions.
Exploring this intersection is one of the primary reasons I study information technology while working in financial education. Software is the highest-leverage lever we have to democratize knowledge.

journals.title: Why I Believe in Learning in Public
journals.excerpt: When I first started creating educational notes on personal finance, I worried about not knowing enough. But documenting what I learn as I go has completely changed how I think, write, and retain ideas. Teaching forces clarity.
journals.author: Aakash Das

content.lead: When I first started creating educational notes on personal finance, my biggest hesitation was feeling unqualified. I asked myself whether someone who is still studying and learning has any right to write explainers. What I discovered is that learning in public is not about claiming authority—it is about documenting curiosity with rigor and humility.

sections.heading: Teaching as a Learning Mechanism
paragraphs: There is an old observation attributed to Richard Feynman: if you cannot explain a concept to a beginner in simple terms, you do not truly understand it yourself. In personal finance, this becomes obvious very quickly. The financial industry is filled with jargon that often obscures basic mathematical truths.

When I sit down to break down a concept—whether it is how compound interest works in an ordinary fixed deposit or how tax brackets apply to someone starting their first job—I am forced to identify every gap in my own logic. You cannot hide behind ambiguity when you are writing for an audience of peers.

sections.heading: Honesty Over Performance
paragraphs: The internet often rewards the appearance of expertise. People feel pressured to present themselves as finished products with all the answers. But I have found that honesty is infinitely more sustainable. When I write "Here is what I currently understand, and here are the questions I am still exploring," it opens up genuine conversations.

Learning in public invites feedback. Thoughtful readers point out edge cases, recommend better source material, and challenge underlying assumptions. That feedback loop accelerates understanding in a way that isolated private study never could.
sections.quote: You do not need to be at the destination to point out the trail markers you just passed.

sections.heading: Building a Compounding Archive
paragraphs: Every essay, checklist, and spreadsheet I publish becomes a small permanent asset in an evolving intellectual portfolio. Looking back at work from six months ago allows me to measure personal growth with tangible evidence.
For anyone hesitant to share their work: the goal is not to be the definitive voice on a topic. The goal is simply to be a reliable, thoughtful explorer documenting the journey with care.
